chat.text: Establish a durable AI-system mastermind in `public/framework/ai/` that can answer how the system works and help improve its architecture. It should map the full AI/session ecosystem—Servex, voice and Whisper, agent launch, prompts, instructions, skills, and their triggers—starting from a top-down README architecture map. Investigate how startup context can automatically include current system state and the README chain from repository root to each agent's primary working directory. Keep it separate from the Core/Page domain mastermind pilot.

message.text: Add requirement: track each mastermind and its sessions with cost, session name, and live/running status, then surface this as a configurable data-grid card in the relevant page chat. Treat custom chat cards as an architectural deliverable; inspect existing card/chat systems and cost logs first, and distinguish what's already available from gaps.

Explore a dedicated AI/session page with a Chat tab, while preserving the existing mobile AI rail button and its pop-up sheet. The full-page experience should complement the mobile sheet, not replace it.

The owner is unsure whether `/framework/ai/` is the right home for a dedicated chat/session page. Leave the location undecided pending architecture review; the mobile rail button and sheet should remain regardless.

Add a reusable system/session-template objective: discover how system prompts, skills, startup instructions, worktree/server use, browser/Playwright testing, and long-lived domain masterminds are configured; design a safe reusable template before changing working configuration. The owner wants distinct Page, AI, and Dictate domain masterminds and a predictable way to start each.

System-template requirement sharpened: create a way to revise the integrated system configuration without obliterating a different working system—preserve a known-good baseline and make versions/experiments isolated and reversible.

Scope note: the system architecture crosses the client, Server, Servex, and AI runtimes/providers (local and cloud). A safe system template must account for those boundaries; experiments that change server behavior may require an isolated server fork, not only a UI worktree.

Refine launch-policy goal: not merely permitting three domain-specific masterminds. Establish a safe, general capability for the smart assistant to launch appropriate independent agents from refined requests—especially task masterminds that own a task and can manage their own workers—without turning the smart assistant into a minion manager. Review trusted caller identity, allowed roles, provider enforcement, task/worktree setup, and tests; keep ordinary worker restrictions intact.
